title: First-Mile Onramp: Catalyst Retail Pilot Brief
content:
Purpose
This brief captures the kickoff plan, technical onboarding checklist, acceptance criteria, and early workshop output for the Catalyst Retail pilot. Goal is to validate a production pattern for embedding-driven product search and a lightweight assistant for store ops using Redwood Hosted API and a Dedicated fallback.

Context
Catalyst Retail (simulated customer) wants to:
- Improve in-store product lookup accuracy for associates (voice + text).
- Deploy an assistant for inventory checks and basic troubleshooting.
- Run an initial 30-day pilot integrated with their POS and internal product catalog.

Constraints and assumptions (initial)
- Data: product catalog (CSV -> S3), POS event stream (Kafka), no PII in pilot data.
- Security: use Redwood Hosted initially behind a private API key; Dedicated reserved capacity considered if latency or throughput needs spike.
- SLA for pilot: target 95% of requests < 350ms tail latency for single-turn queries.
- Budget: 2,000 USD/week (trial credit + pilot budget) for hosting + embeddings.

Stakeholders
- Catalyst Retail: Priya Shah (Product Lead), Omar Rahman (Ops)
- Redwood: Elena Park (SE owner), Mateo Alvarez (Platform eng liaison), Jordan Kim (SDK/DevEx)
- Success contact: Sara Nguyen (Customer Success)

Kickoff objectives (week 0–1)
1) Align on success metrics and acceptance criteria.
2) Provision sample dataset and confirm connectivity (S3 read + sandbox POS events).
3) Run an end-to-end smoke test: catalog -> embeddings -> search API -> assistant prompt flow.
4) Workshop: define 10 canonical queries and 20 eval prompts for quality guardrails.

Workshop agenda (90min on Day 1)
- 0–10 min: Introductions + pilot scope overview (Elena)
- 10–30 min: Customer context: POS flows, busiest queries, store-edge constraints (Catalyst)
- 30–50 min: Architecture options: hosted vs dedicated vs private (Mateo)
- 50–75 min: Define acceptance criteria and top 10 queries (interactive)
- 75–90 min: Immediate next steps + action owners (Sara)

Architecture notes (working)
- Primary: Redwood Hosted API (text gen + embeddings) in us-west region.
- Fallback plan: Redwood Dedicated pool reserved for weekend peak events if latency > 500ms for >5% p99.
- Caching: prefix cache + embedding vector cache at edge (CDN) for product metadata.
- Batching: client SDK to enable small micro-batches for embedding/egress to optimize cost.

Integration checklist (tech tasks)
- [ ] Customer to provide sample product catalog export (CSV) and schema mapping (by day 2).
- [ ] Generate baseline embeddings using open model recommended in catalog doc (se-embed-small-v1) and store vector index (day 3).
- [ ] Map POS event webhooks to staging endpoint and ensure JSON schema stable (day 4).
- [ ] Implement assistant flow skeleton: prompt template, tool calling for product lookup, confidence threshold gating (day 5).
- [ ] Instrument telemetry: latency histograms, token counts, errors, and quality labels (day 7).
- [ ] Add test harness for the 20 eval prompts and track QA pass rate per model version (day 7).

Acceptance criteria (must pass to consider pilot successful)
- Functional: assistant returns correct product SKU or top-3 suggestions for >= 85% of canonical queries (from workshop set).
- Latency: 95th percentile latency for assistant text responses < 350ms in normal traffic; p99 < 800ms.
- Cost: average cost per assisted query < 0.25 USD (token+embed amortized) in pilot workload simulation.
- Stability: < 0.5% error rate (4xx/5xx) for inference endpoints during business hours.
- Integrations: automated ingestion pipeline completes daily catalog sync with no manual steps.

Quality guardrails and evals
- Create 3 quality buckets: ExactMatch (SKU match), Relevant (correct product but different SKU), Miss (irrelevant).
- Evals: run 20 prompt set daily after model changes and gate deploys if overall accuracy drops > 5% vs baseline.
- Monitoring: set alerts on quality regression tied to commit/PRs and model rollouts.

Runbook: common issues + quick fixes (pilot-specific)
- Missing embeddings: re-run ingestion job -> check for malformed CSV rows (common cause).
- High latency: check batching window & KV cache hit rate; if low, temporarily route to Dedicated pool as fallback.
- Token cost spike: inspect prompt template size and recent changes; revert to compact prompts if needed.

Risks and open questions (notes to self)
- Q1: If POS events include PII, need encryption + Private deployment discussion; escalate to Security.
- Q2: Catalog size growth >500k SKUs will need vector sharding and index tuning; plan for offline scale test.
- Risk: Retail network at stores can be flaky — consider local edge caching and degrade to last-known-state responses.

Success measurement cadence
- Daily: ingestion health and eval job results summary (automated email).
- Weekly: 30-min sync with Catalyst product & ops to review metrics and blockers.
- End of 30 days: run final evaluation across 1,000 realistic queries and produce pilot summary (metrics + recommendation).

Deliverables by end of pilot (expected)
- E2E demo video + reproducible runbook.
- Eval report: accuracy, latency, cost breakdown, regression notes.
- Recommendation memo: continue hosted, move to Dedicated, or evaluate Private deployment.

Immediate next actions (assigned)
- Catalyst: export sample catalog and provide schema mapping (Priya) — due 2024-11-08.
- Redwood (Elena): provision staging API key, sample ingestion job, share skeleton prompt templates — due 2024-11-07.
- Platform (Mateo): prepare a Dedicated-capacity quote if pilot shows >2k qps — due 2024-11-12.
- DevEx (Jordan): prepare SDK snippet + mini integration guide for POS webhook connector — due 2024-11-09.

Notes and friction points to monitor during pilot
- Tokenization differences between embedding and generation models can cause mismatch in similarity thresholds — watch for false negatives.
- If customer wants on-prem from day 1, need to surface compliance work and Private offering lead time (4–6 weeks).

Appendix: quick eval prompt examples (selected)
- "Which SKU matches 'red cotton polo size M' and is available in aisle 7?"
- "Customer on phone: recommended similar items to SKU 34321 for cold-weather layering."
- "Store associate: where is the box of barcode labels stored?"
- "Is SKU 881 in stock at store 209?"

Draft retrospective items to think about post-pilot
- How effective was embedding + rerank vs call to product microservice?
- Cost-benefit of prefix caching for frequent queries.
- Improvements in prompt templates for short voice queries (reduce tokens).

Contact and escalation path
- Day-to-day: Elena Park (elena.park@redwood.ai)
- Technical escalations: Mateo Alvarez (mateo@redwood.ai)
- CS escalation: Sara Nguyen (sara@redwood.ai)

---
This doc is intentionally compact. Use it as the working baseline for the Catalyst Retail pilot kickstart. Add notes below as workshop output accumulates.
